cur:catacombs-maius-virgin-child-orans.summary: In an arcosolium lunette a veiled woman with large eyes raises her hands in prayer, a child placed before her breast, between two chi-rho monograms. The painting has long been celebrated as one of the earliest images of the Virgin Mary with the Christ Child in prayer, a forerunner of the later 'Virgin of the Sign'.
facts: The chi-rho monograms – the first letters of Christ's name in Greek – flank the figure on both sides.
Commons classifies the image among 4th-century paintings of the Madonna and Child and among images of the 'Theotokos of the Sign' type.
cur:catacombs-maius-virgin-child-orans.notes: Many scholars think the woman may be the deceased with her child rather than the Virgin and Christ; the identification remains uncertain.
